title: Validate input videos before segmentation
user_visible_behavior: CLI and GUI runs reject missing, unreadable, or unsupported video inputs with a clear error before starting expensive pose extraction.
evidence_plan: CLI preflights inputs via validate_video before pose extraction and exits with a clear error.
GUI upload rejects non-video and missing-field requests with 4xx JSON errors.
Unit + e2e coverage for corrupt, unsupported, too-short, and missing inputs.
evidence: 2026-07-04: src/runtime/video_validation.py validates by content (PyAV probe), not extension; cli.main.run_pipeline preflights via validate_video (min duration vs seq_len/fps) and returns exit 1 with a clear message; GUI /api/upload-and-start rejects non-video and missing-field uploads. Tests green in CI run 28692435270 (all 6 jobs, 3 OSes): tests/test_video_validation.py, tests/test_gui_e2e.py::test_upload_rejects_non_video, ::test_upload_rejects_missing_field, tests/test_cli_pipeline_smoke.py short-video rejection.

title: Split core contracts, analysis engine, API services, and playback contracts
user_visible_behavior: CLI, desktop, browser GUI, and future clients can share one runtime/API contract while preserving current CLI and GUI behavior.
evidence_plan: Branch refactor/runtime-api-engine is based on shipped feat/first-release and main remains untouched until parity is proven.
rallyclip_core imports stay lightweight and own contracts, intervals, pipeline selection, and pure playback scheduling.
rallyclip_engine owns model-object analysis execution from preprocessing through CSV-ready intervals.
rallyclip_api provides a service facade used by Flask routes.
Current CLI smoke/config, GUI smoke/e2e, startup import, native playback, and video-validation tests pass.
evidence: 2026-07-04: COMPLETE and merged to main. rallyclip_core (contracts, intervals, pipeline resolution, SavedMatchStore, playback scheduling), rallyclip_engine (AnalysisModel preprocess/infer/postprocess, manifest-driven pipeline selection), rallyclip_api (RallyClipServices facade + JSON serialization). CLI and Flask GUI are both thin facade clients; CLI gained --json. Golden CLI parity on committed fixture (byte-exact same-machine; 0.25s cross-platform bar). Landed via PR #24 (fcda361) and PR #25 (ed39983); main == feat/first-release. CI matrix (3 OS x test/e2e) fully green for the first time in repo history (run 28692435270). Also fixed en route: issue #21 A/V sync drift (336ms -> 0.3ms, per-interval seek + sample-granular audio reconciliation), jobs_lock status/cancel race caught by the new concurrency hammer test, PyAV consolidated as the only runtime video decoder.
notes: Done. Follow-on tracked separately: onnx-pose-runner-swap, frozen-app e2e tiers, CI dependency lockfile, gui.app config-object injection (retire module-global monkeypatching).

README-documented flags parse; --json emits the stable RunResult payload.

evidence: 2026-06-28: PYTHONPATH=src import probe showed gui.app imports in 0.216s with torch/ultralytics/av/numpy all unloaded. Tests passed: tests/test_gui_startup_imports.py; tests/test_gui_smoke.py::test_gui_health_and_defaults; tests/test_gui_smoke.py::test_gui_pipeline_streams_features_into_inference; tests/test_gui_e2e.py::test_config_defaults_contract; tests/test_gui_e2e.py::test_upload_rejects_non_video; tests/test_gui_e2e.py::test_upload_rejects_missing_field; tests/test_gui_e2e.py::test_default_job_completes. 2026-06-30: packaged Mac release on feat/first-release was built, Developer ID signed with hardened runtime, notarized by Apple, stapled, mounted, and Gatekeeper accepted the app from the DMG. Replay/library startup no longer imports analysis/transcode stack, /api/config/defaults is static, New Match warmup runs in a child process, and upload jobs run in an analysis worker subprocess so Torch/YOLO memory exits after completion/cancel. Production Mac replay uses native source playback; automatic proxy/HLS playback is not part of v0.1.0. Remaining separate tracked work: runtime-video-validation, ONNX/Ultralytics replacement, bundle slimming, CI/CD, and shared runtime/API restructuring. Entitlement-fixed GitHub release DMG was downloaded, installed, and opened successfully; the previous notarized DMG must not ship.

title: Stabilize rally interval decoding
user_visible_behavior: Frame probabilities decode into tennis rally intervals with stable thresholds, minimum duration handling, and CSV/video output timing.
evidence_plan: Gaussian + hysteresis decode with min-duration handling produces stable intervals on the golden fixture.
Exported segment video stays lip-synced across many cuts.
evidence: 2026-07-04: golden CLI parity locks decode output on the committed fixture (byte-exact same-machine; 0.25s cross-platform tolerance = one 0.2s hysteresis hop, the measured torch-version noise floor). Issue #21 fixed: segment_video rewritten to per-interval seek+decode with sample-granular audio reconciliation; measured drift 336ms -> 0.3ms over 10 segments (tests/test_segment_av_sync.py). tests/test_segment.py + av-sync suite green in CI run 28692435270.

title: Replace Ultralytics/torch pose inference with a torch-free ONNX runner
user_visible_behavior: Analysis produces identical segments without importing torch or ultralytics at runtime, cutting inference memory (~530MB -> ~155MB class) and enabling opencv-python removal.
evidence_plan: Preprocessing bitwise-equal to Ultralytics rect letterbox at the production contract (imgsz=960, dynamic-axes export).
Decoded contract parity (boxes/conf/keypoints, iou=0.7 NMS, max_det=300, conf-sorted) on a wide frame set.
Full-pipeline segment parity vs torch on the golden clip and 60s samples from all 11 raw match videos.
Memory/perf benchmark at 960; then integrate runner into RallyClip src and demote torch/ultralytics to a dev extra.
evidence: 2026-07-04: shipped on feat/onnx-pose-runner (PR #26). Runner integrated at src/extraction/yolo_onnx_runner.py; manifest-referenced asset models/rallyclip_v0.3.1/yolov8n-pose-960-dynamic.onnx; PoseExtractor and CourtDetector dispatch on weights extension; non-pose ONNX heads raise UnsupportedOnnxOutputShapeError (unit-tested). Parity: preprocessing bitwise-equal; decoded contract IoU >= 0.999997 / kpt err <= 3.1e-4 px; stage-4 sweep 17/17 byte-equal segments (11 raw_videos + 6 testing_app 1080p60 samples), zero count mismatches. torch/ultralytics demoted to [train] extra; golden CLI exit-0 + byte-equal CSV in a fresh venv WITHOUT torch installed. Perf: onnx 19.7s/458MB mean vs torch 28.6s/753MB (60s sample). Report: YOLO-ONNX/parity_960/sweep_report.json; results: RallyClip-perf/docs/onnx-pose-parity-plan.md.
notes: Model export must be at imgsz=960 with dynamic axes (rect letterbox 960x544 for 16:9); Ultralytics NMS defaults iou=0.7/max_det=300. YOLO26 e2e export (NMS in graph) is the strategic alternative.

title: MLX backend so models run fast on Apple hardware
user_visible_behavior: On Apple-silicon Macs, pose + LSTM inference runs on the GPU/ANE via MLX (or an equivalent CoreML execution path), cutting analysis time versus the current CPU-only onnxruntime path, with identical (or tolerance-documented) segment output.
evidence_plan: YOLOv8n-pose and LSTM weights converted to MLX (or CoreML EP) with a documented conversion script.
Golden-clip segments match the onnxruntime CPU path byte-equal or within the documented 0.25s tolerance.
Benchmark on the 17-sample sweep: wall-clock and peak RSS vs onnxruntime CPU recorded.
Runtime selects the accelerated path on Apple silicon and falls back to CPU onnxruntime elsewhere.
Bundle-size impact measured (MLX deps vs onnxruntime).
evidence: Spike complete 2026-07-05 (docs/perf/coreml-spike/ on RallyClip-perf + DECISIONS.md entry): CoreML EP in stock onnxruntime 1.24.4 with a STATIC 544x960 re-export (MLProgram, MLComputeUnits=ALL) runs pose at 120.4 fps vs 15.6 fps shipping CPU path (8.05x); confident-detection divergence 1.2e-4. Dynamic-axes model blocks ANE (only 1.2x). LSTM measured slower on CoreML — stays CPU. Decision: no MLX rewrite; productionize static export + opt-in CoreML provider (CPU stays parity default). Remaining: bundle static export, provider flag + fallback, sweep benchmark, golden tolerance policy.
notes: Requested 2026-07-05. Consider coremltools/onnxruntime-coreml EP as a lower-risk alternative to full MLX rewrite; decide in a spike first. Spike verdict 2026-07-05: CoreML EP wins, MLX rejected.

title: Edit mode: trim/add/delete points, non-destructive
user_visible_behavior: In the library, an Edit mode lets the user drag point boundaries (like trimming a video in iPhone Photos) to extend/shrink a point or shift its times, add a new point, and delete a point. Edits write to a duplicate CSV (segments_edited.csv); the original segments.csv is never modified. When an edited CSV exists, exports and playback use it. A 'Reset to original' button deletes the edited copy and restores original behavior.
evidence_plan: Entering edit mode creates segments_edited.csv as a copy of segments.csv (original untouched, verified byte-equal after edits).
Drag handles adjust a point's start/end; changes persist to the edited CSV via /api/*.
Add-point and delete-point buttons work and persist.
Export video / CSV download use the edited CSV when present, original otherwise.
Reset-to-original removes the edited CSV and the UI reflects original segments.
Playwright e2e covers the full edit->export->reset loop.
evidence: Implemented 2026-07-05 on branch feat/segment-edit-mode (stacked on fix/viewer-direct-playback). Backend: segments_edited.csv precedence in playback manifest//segments//csv//export, PUT /api/library/<id>/segments, DELETE .../segments/edits (reset), export.mp4 invalidated on edit/reset; original segments.csv never written. Frontend: Edit points mode in viewer — drag trim handles on timeline, add/delete point, Reset to original, autosave per edit. Tests: 3 backend unit tests (roundtrip/validation/export-invalidation) + Playwright e2e (trim-drag, add, delete, reset) — 30/30 smoke, 7/7 playwright module green.
notes: Requested 2026-07-05. All behavior through /api/* per architecture invariant; timeline drag UI in the existing frontend player.
